description: Set a .NET project's version to an exact value in every place it must agree — a .NET library, service, or Windows desktop app (WPF, WinUI 3, Windows Forms) alike. Rewrites `<Version>` (or `<VersionPrefix>` + `<VersionSuffix>`) in the root `Directory.Build.props` when it declares one, otherwise in every non-test `*.csproj` that declares one, and the MSIX package identity — `<Identity Version="x.y.z.0">` in every tracked `Package.appxmanifest` (WinUI single-project MSIX) and `packaging/AppxManifest.xml` (WPF/WinForms MSIX) — always as the four-part numeric value derived from the new version (pre-release suffix stripped, revision `0`, as the Microsoft Store requires). Follows this catalog's `x.y.z-dev` development-version convention (Step 5). Uses an embedded, tested Python helper with `--list` and `--dry-run` modes, preserves BOMs and CRLF line endings, never touches test projects or explicit `<AssemblyVersion>`/`<FileVersion>` values (it reports them), and refuses to write when the `<Version>` locations disagree until the user confirms. Invoke as `/iru-dotnet-bump-version <new-version>` where `<new-version>` is the literal target (e.g. `1.4.0` or `1.5.0-dev`) — this skill never computes a bump itself (`iru-release` computes the release/next-dev values per Step 5 and passes each one through). Also accepts `args` (`key: value` lines): `sync-files: yes|no` (default: ask) to also update README/Antora version mentions, `next-version: <upcoming-version>` so that sync maps "Latest release" markers to `<new-version>` and "Current development version" markers to the upcoming value, and `dry-run: yes|no` (default `no`) to print the diff without writing anything. Reports every location found with its old value, the new values, and every file touched. Use whenever the user, or `iru-release` (key `dotnet`), needs a .NET project's version set to a specific value instead of hand-editing MSBuild properties and MSIX manifests.
